angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 452,205 km at 31.59 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 31.6569 +/- 0.0152 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 31.59 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.65 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Barragán et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 73583 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.514.1606B/abstract): 452,205 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.73 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Barragán et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 73583 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.514.1606B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4511 +/- 110 K from Barragán et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 73583 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.514.1606B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barragán et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 73583 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.514.1606B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-73583.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.676, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
